The Co36Fe18Ni18Cr15Al12Mo1 HEA was fabricated by vacuum arc-melting furnace in an argon atmosphere (purity > 99.9 wt%). The ingot was flipped and re-melted at least six times with electromagnetic stirring.
Afterward, the ingot was cold rolled with a thickness reduction ratio of 80% (from 8 to 1.6 mm)
annealed at 700, 800, 900 and 1000 ◦C for 1 h and subsequently water quenched (referred to as A700, A800, A900 and A1000, respectively).

Apparently, both the FCC and BCC/B2 phase were indexed in the annealed alloys.
The A700 and A800 alloys exhibit a complex microstructure consisting of non-recrystallized and recrystallized FCC grains, as well as rod and particle shape B2 precipitates (Fig. 3a1-a2 and b1-b2).
The AC alloy displays a dendrite structure, as shown in Fig. 2a.
Moreover, BCC stringer bands paralleling to the rolling direction are observed from cold-rolled alloy, as shown in Fig. 2b.
The volume fraction of recrystallized region in the A700 and A800 alloys are 12% and 48%, respectively.
The volume fraction of recrystallized region in the A700 and A800 alloys are 12% and 48%, respectively.

The rod-shaped B2 precipitates in A700 and A800 alloy respectively presents an average width of ~13 nm and ~300 nm and aspect ratio of ~7 and ~2.5, and they are distributed within the non-recrystallized FCC grains

The rod-shaped B2 precipitates in A700 and A800 alloy respectively presents an average width of ~13 nm and ~300 nm and aspect ratio of ~7 and ~2.5, and they are distributed within the non-recrystallized FCC grains

As the annealed temperature increase, the A900 and A1000 alloys display a full-recrystallized structure and particle shape B2 precipitates, without the rod-shaped B2 precipitates (Fig. 3c1-d2 and Fig. 5a1-b2).
For the A1000 alloy, the FCC and B2 particles have an average size of ~3.6 and ~1.9 μm respectively.
For the non-recrystallized grain (NRG), dislocation cell containing high-density dislocation were observed, as shown in Fig. 10a.
Substantial stacking faults (SFs) can be observed in the ultra-fine grain of the A700 alloy (Fig. 10b and c).
After fracture, a high density of dislocation was observed near the FCC/B2 interfaces, indicating that the B2 phase is a strong barrier to dislocation motion (Fig. 11b).

A700 shows a high yield strength 1820 ± 22 MPa and uniform tensile strength 1884 ± 21 MPa with a fracture elongation 9.7 ± 2.1%.

The full-recrystallized A900 alloy still remains a high yield strength and ultimate tensile strength of 1038 ± 17 MPa and 1246 ± 18 MPa, respectively.
